title: Five Windows and One Moon
synopsis: The five friends share funny Moon observations at Story House; as the full Moon rises at sunset, each returns to a familiar home with a grown-up.
continuity_state: Before: Across earlier nights Amy saw a narrow crescent, Ben a wider crescent, Kim a half-lit Moon, Wendy a gibbous one, and Todd a nearly full one. No new objects have entered the Story House shelf; the little garden still has plants but no mature flowers. After: At Village Green the five friends meet during an ordinary afternoon, share Moon jokes, and briefly observe a full Moon rising on the eastern side of the sky at sunset. They return to their established homes with grown-ups. Story House shelf still holds blue Book of Little Sounds, brown Button Town envelope, and LITTLE GROWING GARDEN folder; Ben takes cutout paper home. Real map still has no Moon location, and garden leaves are a little bigger without sunflower blooms or harvest. The season is fully resolved.

related_resources.reason: NASA explains that at full Moon the Earth-facing side is maximally sunlit from our viewpoint and the full Moon rises near sunset.
The contrast is original literary characterization. AAP guidance supports optional shared storytelling, not a finding that this specific line induces perspective taking.
